messages:
eli: Heads-up — ran the first INT4 pass on the new compact-embed (seedling-v1) against webq-holdout.
sara: Nice. Quick numbers? :eyes:
eli: Recall@1 dropped ~6.5% vs fp16 on short queries (<= 8 tokens). Recall@10 ~1.2% down.
devin: That gap on short queries smells like normalization or quant noise at small seq lengths.
tim: Do we have per-dimension scale stats? Maybe per-channel quantization mismatch.
eli: I dumped the embed norms: median L2 shifted from 1.02 -> 0.88 under INT4. Distribution skewed.
sara: Oof. Could be clipping from quantization or our post-quant L2 renormalize step not applied consistently.
devin: Can you paste the eval command you ran?
eli: ```
# run locally
python eval/recall.py --model seedling-v1 --quant int4 --dataset webq-holdout --split short --k 1,10 --norm l2
```
sara: benchbot, did you run the same sweep with per-channel vs global scale earlier?
benchbot: benchbot: sweep completed — per-channel INT4 reduced recall drop to ~2.0% on short queries. Full logs at /mnt/bench/347321.
eli: Great, per-channel helps. But still nontrivial gap. Cluster plots show tighter clusters but some anchors moved between neighbors.
tim: Can you share the UMAP snapshot? Tiny visual cues help.
eli: Uploaded image link (not shown here). Quick summary: a few small clusters that were previously single cluster split into two under INT4.
devin: That suggests quantization noise pushes some vectors across border for nearest-neighbor thresholds.
sara: Possible mitigations: re-run with symmetric quant and fine-tune a 1-epoch calibration with MSE loss, or apply last-layer bias correction.
tim: Also try bias/offset correction: compute mean delta between fp16 and quantized embeddings on a calibration set and subtract.
eli: I'll run a quick calibrate test. If cal reduces L2 shift we can re-eval.
eli: Quick result: calibration subtraction recovered ~3.8% out of the 6.5% loss at R@1.
devin: Good. That plus per-channel might get us within 1%.
sara: For release checklist: include calibration table, per-channel vs global numbers, norm-shift plot, and a short blurb about short-query fragility.
tim: Also add a small test in onboarding pipeline to flag >2% R@1 regression on short split.
eli: Agree. I'll open a tiny PR with eval artifacts and a CLI flag for short-split smoke.
sara: Thanks. If regression persists we might need to keep fp16 for short-query-heavy customers.
devin: Tagging @tim for infra quota if we need more calibration runs.
benchbot: benchbot: queued extra GPU slot for 2h (ID: gpu-44) — start when ready.
eli: Starting the per-channel+calib run now. Will update in this thread.
sara: :thumbsup:
